comparator.name: Geografie, Planologie en Milieu
comparator.academicYear: Current published prospective bachelor curriculum, checked 2026-09-25
comparator.route: Globalisation thematic track (18 EC in year two; 6 EC thematic course in year three)
comparator.sourceNotes: A coherent 180-EC illustration uses 60 EC of ten first-year compulsory courses, the 42-EC common second-year curriculum plus the published 18-EC Globalisation track, then the Globalisation third-year course (6 EC), Practising Spatial Theories (6 EC), 30 EC genuinely open elective space and an 18-EC independent thesis. The university offers Urbanisation and Sustainability tracks as alternative choices; their course rows are not mixed into this single comparator. Third-year details are explicitly subject to curriculum change. The open electives are not assigned invented subjects or presented as automatically equivalent to UCR courses; the prior Tallinn/Bilbao fieldwork destinations are examples, not required places.

alternatives.label: People, environments and global change
alternatives.concept: An interdisciplinary human geography response linking societies and global flows to environmental change, governance, spatial data, economics and applied delta research. It offers GIS and environment-related study but does not reproduce a dedicated urban planning degree, geographic fieldwork abroad or professional teaching route.
alternatives.labelReason: Sociology, global economics, international relations, governance, Earth observation and sustainability research substantiate both people and environmental change without claiming a full Geography or Spatial Planning degree.
progression: Introductory sociology, economics, sustainability and methods precede advanced quantitative analysis, governance and project work where offered. The European law prerequisite and all scheduled semester offerings are satisfied.

alternatives.label: Environmental transitions and delta resilience
alternatives.concept: A distinct environmental-science and sustainability pathway through Earth systems, climate, ecology, coastal hazards, water governance, renewable energy, circularity and applied delta research, with social research and environmental justice. It does not reproduce the Radboud dedicated spatial-planning and urbanisation curriculum.
alternatives.labelReason: The selected Earth science, climate, ecology, environmental governance, water and renewable systems courses sustain a different scientific focus from the first programme.
progression: Sustainability Essentials I precedes II and formal 300-level dependencies; Earth and climate courses provide introductory grounding before advanced resources and energy study. The six published semester offerings and prerequisites are satisfied.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the first programme, this pathway replaces more than eight economics, European politics, law and global-society courses with Earth-system methods, ecology, hazards, water, circularity and renewable-energy study; the inquiry and specialist 300-level depth change substantially.

candidates.label: Urbanisation and spatial planning
candidates.reason: Radboud offers a coherent Urbanisation track, but UCR Spatial Planning and Public Policy Analysis have no X in any of the six planned semesters. The available courses in comparative politics, public economics, social theory and nature-based building do not supply sustained urban design, land development, planning law and transport geography across a distinct 24-course programme. These are explicit gaps in the broad first alternative.

candidates.label: Secondary-school geography teaching
candidates.reason: The university describes an optional 30-EC Educative Minor with school teaching practice; the UCR catalogue contains no teacher-training placement or geography teaching qualification.

routeSelection.route: Globalisation thematic track (18 EC in year two; 6 EC thematic course in year three)
routeSelection.basis: The published 42+18 second-year structure and 6+6+30+18 third-year structure form one internally coherent 180-EC path, and Globalisation is the first formally listed track on the year-two programme page when no route is specified in the registry. Urbanisation and Sustainability remain real alternative Radboud tracks, not credits combined with this comparator.

selection.assessment: Two feasible, substantively different UCR curricula cover global social-environmental change and environmental transitions. A third urban-planning curriculum would rely on unscheduled planning/policy courses and unrelated substitutions; the teaching option also lacks formal teacher education.

notes.text: UCR combines relevant social sciences, environmental science, GIS and delta research. Radboud GPM supplies a dedicated sequence in human geography, spatial planning, urbanisation, quantitative and qualitative fieldwork, and a geography-specific thesis; the UCR alternatives are related academic paths rather than equivalent credentials.
